subject: Follow-up: hit-rate breakdown and burn-rate qualification
body_excerpt: Recap of today's discovery with hit-rate sensitivity buckets and requested customer confirmation on volumes and realistic prefix-hit expectations.
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sally Kim <sally.kim@atlas-retail.com>, Atlas Retail Ops <ops@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: hit-rate breakdown and burn-rate qualification

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and a few asks so we can model realistic unit economics for Atlas.

Key points from the call:
- Monthly token expectation (your estimate): ~500M tokens/mo (you mentioned the 400–600M range).
- Primary workloads: product search + guided chat (heavy shared prefixes due to templated flows).
- Budget sensitivity: you called out a target effective spend in the ballpark of $6k–$12k/mo (high-level).

Why the hit-rate question matters:
- Our pricing model for this exercise uses a baseline generation cost for the chosen model and then applies a prefix cache hit-rate to convert gross token usage into an effective billed token volume.
- Small changes in hit rate (e.g., 20% -> 40%) materially change the effective $/1M tokens and monthly burn.

Attached: hit_rate_model_v1.xlsx and a one-page pricing calc (redwood_pricing_calc.pdf). The workbook contains three scenarios we sketched during the call: No cache (0% hit), Moderate (30% hit), High (60% hit). For each we list: gross tokens, cached tokens, effective billed tokens, and resulting monthly cost.

Quick asks (so we can finalize a tailored quote):
1) Can you confirm the working monthly range (best/worst) for tokens? We used 400M / 600M for the attached.
2) How many of your user flows are template-led? (Rough percent — e.g., 50% of sessions follow 5 fixed templates). That drives prefix cache expectations.
3) Can you share a 1-day sample of anonymized session traces (token counts per session) or allow us to run a short sampling script?

Proposed next step: 30-minute model-run with Ben (solutions) to plug in your traces and show a 2x/3x sensitivity table. Are you available Tue/Wed next week?

Thanks — I’ll hold a slot and Ben will run the workbook live.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: hit_rate_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_pricing_calc.pdf (one-pager)

From: Sally Kim <sally.kim@atlas-retail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hit-rate breakdown and burn-rate qualification

Thanks Vanessa — great session. Quick answers to your asks: 
- Monthly range: we expect 450M typical, with peaks to ~700M in promo months. Baseline for modeling: use 450M / 700M.
- Template-led flows: roughly 45% of sessions use a handful of canned prompts (search+filter shortcuts). So a 30–40% prefix hit looks plausible, 60% probably optimistic unless we implement aggressive normalization.
- We can provide a 48-hour anonymized dump (tokens/session + flow id); I'll need to clear with legal for a sanitized extract. Ops can share by EOD Friday.

For budget: the $6k–$12k/mo was a rough internal cap per feature team. We want to understand whether that can map to a sustained 500–600M tokens monthly with reasonable hit rates.

Happy to do Tue morning for the modeling session — Ben’s participation sounds good.

—
Sally Kim
Director, Product Analytics | Atlas Retail
sally.kim@atlas-retail.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sally Kim <sally.kim@atlas-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hit-rate breakdown and burn-rate qualification

On Thu, Jun 2, 2027 at 12:15 PM Sally Kim <sally.kim@atlas-retail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Vanessa — great session. Quick answers to your asks: 
> - Monthly range: we expect 450M typical, with peaks to ~700M in promo months.
> - Template-led flows: roughly 45% of sessions use a handful of canned prompts ...
>
Thanks — that helps a lot. I ran the quick scenarios in the attached workbook; excerpt below (numbers rounded):

Baseline inputs used for the table (we agreed these on the call):
- Gross tokens (monthly): 450,000,000
- Reference model unit cost (list for this quote): $1,100 per 1M generated tokens (we used a model-specific list price for the chosen model variant)

Scenario math (illustrative):
- No cache (0% hit): billed tokens = 450M -> monthly cost = $495,000 -> effective $/1M = $1,100
- Moderate cache (30% hit): billed tokens = 315M -> monthly cost = $346,500 -> effective $/1M = $770 (calculation: 346,500 / 315 -> $1,100 * 0.7 = $770)
- High cache (60% hit): billed tokens = 180M -> monthly cost = $198,000 -> effective $/1M = $1,100 * 0.4 = $440

Interpretation:
- With your 45% templated flows, a midpoint cache hit of ~35% is a realistic planning assumption today. That implies an effective $/1M closer to ~$715–$800 in our workbook depending on routing and micro-caching of recent contexts.
- To reach your $6k–$12k/mo target ranges per team, we'd need either: a) much higher cache rates (70%+), b) a lower-cost model variant, c) significant per-request routing to cheaper tiers for lower-priority traffic.

Next steps I’ll run before our session:
- Ben to sanity-check the workbook and add a peak-month sensitivity (450M -> 700M).
- If you can share the 48-hour anonymized traces, we’ll produce a per-flow hit-rate estimate and a recommended prefix sizing strategy.

Proposed meeting: Tue 2027-06-08 09:30 PT (30m) — Ben to demo the workbook in real time. Please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Attachments: hit_rate_model_v1.xlsx (updated)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

I also added a short checklist in the workbook: fields we need for the sim (session_id, tokens_in_prompt, flow_template_id).
